title: Copy machine run invariant
statement: Let $x$ be a Boolean word. For every $t\in\mathbb{N}$ with $t\le |x|$, after $t$ steps from the copy machine's initial configuration on $x$, the machine remains in its unique state, its input head is at position $t+1$, and its output is the prefix of $x$ of length $t$.
replaced:
Let $x$ be a Boolean word and run the one-state copy machine from its initial
configuration on input $x$.  For every $t \le \abs{x}$, after $t$ steps the
machine is still live in its unique state, its input head sits at position
$t + 1$ (in the convention where position $0$ is the left boundary blank and
position $j$ with $1 \le j \le \abs{x}$ scans the $j$-th input symbol), and its
output is exactly the first $t$ symbols of $x$.
